purpose: private authored activity pilot; not learner-facing

activities.cueEnglish: Find what the witness says happened at the end of the day.
activities.modelFrench: Kevin a dit qu’en fin de journée tout le monde était fatigué et que personne n’avait vérifié la bâche.
activities.modelEnglish: Kevin said that at the end of the day everyone was tired and that nobody checked the tarp.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name a misunderstanding in French.
Listen and identify the French term for tie-down.
Type 'One at a time, please.' in French.
activities.modelFrench: Un à la fois, s’il vous plaît.

activities.cueEnglish: Ask Marcos to tell his side of the story.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Marcos, d’accord, raconte-moi ta version. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: Marcos, OK, tell me your side.

activities.cueEnglish: Write the new tarp-check assignment before the crew leaves.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Désormais, désignons une personne qui vérifie les attaches selon le plan et m’envoie une photo avant le départ. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: From today, designate someone to check the tarp tie-downs under the site plan and send me a photo before leaving.

activities.cueEnglish: Find the water and electrolytes planned for the crew.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Il y aura de l’eau fraîche dans la glacière toute la journée, ainsi que des électrolytes. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: There will be cold water in the cooler all day, and electrolytes too.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name heat exhaustion in French.
Listen and identify the French term for heatstroke.
Type 'If you get dizzy, tell me right away.' in French.
activities.modelFrench: Si vous avez des étourdissements, prévenez-moi tout de suite.
activities.modelEnglish: If you get dizzy, tell me right away.

activities.cueEnglish: Explain the planned shaded breaks to the crew.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Nous prendrons les pauses prévues à l’ombre; personne ne les sautera pour rattraper le temps. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: We'll take the planned breaks in the shade, and nobody will skip them to catch up.

activities.cueEnglish: Write what Rogelio says about Friday's deadline.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Nous visons vendredi, mais nous ne sacrifierons pas la sécurité pour tenir ce délai. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: We aim for Friday, but we won't sacrifice safety for the deadline.

activities.cueEnglish: Find how Rogelio would speak to a colleague who accepts informal address.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « À un collègue qui accepte le tutoiement, je dirais : Regarde, nous avons trouvé du bois dégradé; viens voir. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: To a colleague who accepts informal address, I say: Look, we found rotten wood; come see.

activities.cueEnglish: Without looking, name the degree of formality in French.
Listen and identify the French term for courtesy.
Type 'Would you allow me to show you the area?' in French.
activities.modelFrench: Pourriez-vous me permettre de vous montrer la zone ?
activities.modelEnglish: Would you allow me to show you the area?

activities.cueEnglish: Ask an older coworker which form of address they prefer.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Demande-lui poliment : Préférez-vous que je vous tutoie ou que je vous vouvoie ? »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: Then ask politely: Do you prefer that I address you informally or formally?

activities.cueEnglish: Write the polite opening Rogelio suggests for the homeowner.
activities.modelFrench: Rogelio : « Je dirais : Excusez-moi de vous déranger, madame; je voudrais vous signaler ce que nous avons trouvé. »
activities.modelEnglish: Rogelio: To her I say: Sorry to bother you, ma'am; I'd like to mention something we found.
